notes: identify-runtime: TIE, 5/5 both arms — zero discrimination. The guile-vs-guile3 version trap is prominently documented in this repo's own README.org, so a baseline that reads the repo gets it right without the skill.
start-and-trace-fib: TIE, 5/5 both arms — zero discrimination. --debug's necessity for ,trace is likewise called out in README.org/EXPERIMENTS.org, independent of the skill.

stale-listener-diagnose: TIE, 5/5 both arms — zero discrimination. Both arms ran --status first and correctly diagnosed 'proxy up, repl down' as the fault before touching anything, entirely from ordinary operational caution. Note: this eval's assertions were originally phrased around a stale-proxy-writing-to-a-different-log fault variant; the fault actually staged here (repl process died, proxy masks it) satisfies the same assertions in substance but not in literal mechanism — worth re-checking this eval's assertions against the fault it's actually paired with.

decline-remote-bind: with_skill 5/6 vs baseline 4/6 — the one eval in this skill with real discrimination. with_skill actually issued the portclaim GET call (and noticed/flagged that its response looked suspiciously real for a sandbox with 'no service'), where baseline skipped even the GET and went straight to a hypothetical POST description. Both correctly declined to widen the bind and recommended an SSH tunnel.

Overall: guile-repl-server's measurable value against a Sonnet-5-class baseline is concentrated almost entirely in the portclaim registration step (eval 4) — the guile3 trap, the --debug requirement, and stale-listener diagnosis are all things a capable baseline already gets right from this repo's own README/EXPERIMENTS.org, independent of the skill file.
